name: pivot_point_breakout_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Classic pivot points (P, R1, R2, S1, S2) calculated from the previous day's OHLC data serve as widely-watched support and resistance levels. When price breaks through R1 or S1 with volume, it signals that the previous day's value area is being exceeded — a meaningful move beyond yesterday's equilibrium. The edge exists because pivot points are a Schelling point: thousands of traders and algorithms watch the same levels, making them self-fulfilling. When R1 breaks, all traders watching it know it has broken, and their collective response (stop-loss triggers, new entries) amplifies the move. The inefficiency is not that pivots are unknown, but that most traders use them as static levels; the edge comes from combining the pivot break with volume confirmation and VWAP alignment to filter false breakouts.
mechanism: Consolidation periods accumulate resting orders above resistance and below support. A breakout triggers these resting orders as stop-losses and breakout entries fire simultaneously. The resulting order flow imbalance overwhelms the resting liquidity, and market makers widen spreads in the breakout direction, accelerating the move.

exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back below R1 (longs) or above S1 (shorts) for 2 bars

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — pivots are structural levels that work across VIX regimes

weaknesses: Pivot point calculation is identical for all participants — zero information edge; edge must come from filters only
In narrow-range days, R1 and S1 may be very close to the open, leading to noisy breaks that quickly reverse
The 2-bar confirmation filter causes late entry — by the time R1 break is confirmed, price may already be near R2
prior_art: Pivot points originated from floor traders (pre-electronic era). Widely documented in TA textbooks and used by virtually all intraday traders globally. Person ('A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics', 2004) covers pivot strategies extensively. Zerodha Varsity covers pivot point strategies for Indian markets specifically.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
